oracleRisk.summary: YUSD has no borrower liquidation branches. Both native AegisMinting deployments use Chainlink collateral USD prices and a configured Aegis YUSD/USD oracle to bound redemption collateral amounts. SETTINGS_MANAGER_ROLE can replace the Aegis oracle, whose operator can directly set the YUSD/USD price and whose owner can appoint operators. Ethereum block 26097119 and BSC block 125091227 on 2026-10-01 confirm nonzero configured oracle addresses. This is discretionary top-level price authority, not automatic balance-derived share accounting.

branchApplicability.reviewer: OpenAI Codex W1b oracle applicability review
branchApplicability.rationale: Aegis's YUSD strategy uses BTC spot collateral and COIN-M perpetuals whose hedge and reserve operations depend on BTC spot/perpetual marks to keep the dollar value stable. This is a price-sensitive top-level internal strategy authority, not a borrower liquidation branch; YUSD has no borrower-owned debt or collateral liquidation paths, so the disposition is top-level-only.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: Ethereum and BSC native YUSD use chain-local AegisMinting and burn/mint OFT adapters; Avalanche and Katana retain their earlier LayerZero route reviews. The expanded issuer deployment census registers Arbitrum, Base, Monad, Plasma, Starknet, and Hedera, including deployed zero-supply tokens. Arbitrum/Base verified YUSDOFT source and Plasma's immutable-masked runtime match prove direct burn/mint without canonical escrow. Starknet's verified mint/burn adapter source and pinned token/role bindings likewise prove direct burn/mint. Monad's different runtime remains source-unbound, and Hedera cannot be read through the required pinned helper despite successful keyless secondary identity reads. Whole-asset independent-liability eligibility remains withdrawn; older controls and Katana source-provenance limits are not refreshed by this census.

The OFT burns on source debit and mints on LayerZero credit; this is an external-validated burn/mint route, not lock/mint.

Re-verified at Katana block 40173492 on 2026-08-16: the same YUSDOFT address is deployed on Katana with endpoint() = LayerZero EndpointV2 0x6f475642a6e85809b1c36fa62763669b1b48dd5b, owner() and EndpointV2.delegates(YUSD) = the Aegis Safe, sharedDecimals() = 6, and peers for Ethereum, BSC, and Avalanche EIDs 30101/30102/30106. The current code size is 13,161 bytes and supply was 0.239979 YUSD. It burns on source debit and mints on LayerZero credit; Katana bytecode is not explorer-verified, so exact source provenance remains an evidence gap.

Issuer manifest identifies YUSDOFT. At Arbitrum block 513233920 (hash 0x04496d65afb73f84cb148bb85bd33e343437ed311ff23b9b1de3a5495701a7eb, timestamp 2026-10-09T15:10:17Z), helper reads return name/symbol YUSD, decimals 18, supply 10.090001 YUSD, token() equal to this deployment, approvalRequired() false, endpoint 0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fe728c, and owner 0x4fe78ef65bd8edded480efab030ba680646503c8. Sourcify verifies YUSDOFT and its inherited OFT._debit calls _burn while _credit calls _mint. YUSDOFT only adds blacklist hooks; it does not replace these paths with lock/release or canonical-supply escrow. This establishes direct burn/mint, not an independent native collateral-mint route or a whole-asset census.

Zero supply is deployment presence, not absence.
